projects.description: The UNDP Green Energy Recovery Programme is an integrated approach to address Ukraine’s needs to accelerate efforts towards a more diverse energy mix, following the impact of the war and outdated energy system. The Programme supports achieving objectives and priorities indicated in the National Energy Strategy, contributing to energy security and independence, supporting a green recovery and transition of the energy sector, promoting decarbonisation and facilitating further synchronisation with the EU energy markets.

projects.name: Education service providers have strengthened capacities to deliver effective education and training opportunities which foster children's well-being
projects.description:
Working with authorities and education service providers primarily at local level, the output will tackle the gaps in the access and quality of educational services which affect learning and skills development, especially for vulnerable children, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. Through technical assistance, modelling, capacity building and direct support and financing for the delivery of supplies and rehabilitation, UNICEF will support the delivery of comprehensive programmes and service packages, strengthening local education systems’ capacities, mechanisms and structures at central and local levels that respond to humanitarian and long-term recovery needs to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	Cost-effective, inclusive early childhood education models are available for implementation in diverse community settings.
•	There is a scalable model supporting young people's transition from learning pathways to first job experiences.
•	Student learning support services are integrated within the General Secondary Education system, providing adaptive remedial education interventions at scale.
•	Teacher training service providers are able to deliver on inclusive education reform.
•	A safe and inclusive digital learning environment supports children, including adolescents, acquisition of learning and skills, including climate action and environmental sustainability.
•	Safe and inclusive learning environments are accessible for conflict affected children.
•	Career-guidance systems within formal and non-formal education and training services (formal and alternative learning pathways) are labour market-informed, stigma-free and gender transformative and facilitate young people's transition from learning to earning.
•	Demonstration of youth skills development approaches within human capital development priority for Ukraine's recovery plan.
•	Increased opportunities for children and youth to choose their preferred career path within Ukraine.

projects.name: Local governments, utilities, educational and health-care institutions have increased capacities to provide quality and sustainable WASH services to vulnerable children and communities.
projects.description:
This Programme output delivers direct support and life-saving supplies and services to affected populations while building national and local capacities for efficient and equitable WASH services, response to climate change and environmental sustainability and equipping institutions with capacities and infrastructure to safeguard children's health and wellbeing, especially in humanitarian contexts. Under this output, UNICEF will provide evidence-based policy advice, technical assistance and modeling as well as direct support and financial assistance at central and decentralized levels to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	Innovative pilots for the provision of quality and equitable water supply services are implemented and available for scaling up.
•	National and local capacities are enhanced for efficient and equitable management of wastewater treatment, sanitation and water supply services empowering children with a safe environment, including in humanitarian contexts. 
•	Key institutions for children have child-friendly, disability-inclusive and gender-responsive WASH infrastructure with appropriate maintenance in the long-term.
•	National and local capacities are enhanced for efficient and equitable response to climate change and environmental sustainability to safeguard children's health and wellbeing.

projects.name: National and local institutional and community capacities are strengthened to provide quality risk- informed, gender-transformative inclusive and shock-responsive child protection and social services for vulnerable children
projects.description:
Through the Programme output, UNICEF will work to close the gaps in service provision and strengthen institutional and community capacities for the delivery of quality, gender- and shock-responsive child protection services and monitoring children’s rights especially for children affected by armed conflict and other humanitarian contexts. Focusing on the implementation of decentralized scalable demonstration models, capacity strengthening, advocacy and policy advice, the output will be implemented primarily at the local level with national outreach and scalability on aim at the following systemic changes:
•	There are tested scalable models for the provision of continuum of care, ECI and support to CwD, their parents/caregivers and service frontline workers.
•	There is an improved availability and state capacity to undertake regular monitoring of children in family-based alternative care.
•	There are established operational mechanisms and packages for the implementation of Minimum Integrated Social Service and Benefits package, including diverse specialized services such as CPiE and GBViE, return and reintegration, children in contact with law, MHPSS and resilience services and the like.

projects.name: Green industrial recovery is facilitated through technology transfer from and co-creation of new businesses with Japan's private industries
projects.description: This large-scale project, funded by the Government of Japan, supports the green industrial recovery of Ukraine by promoting technology transfer from Japanese private industries and the co-creation of innovative businesses between Ukrainian and Japanese partners. It facilitates collaboration across a wide range of industrial sectors, including agribusiness, circular economy, digital technologies, sustainable energy, hydrogen, and micro, small and medium-sized enterprise productivity enhancement. Through skills development, knowledge transfer and dedicated grant and matchmaking mechanisms, the project fosters the creation of new businesses, job creation and the development of a national innovation ecosystem, thereby contributing to inclusive and sustainable industrial development in Ukraine.

projects.description: WFP will provide temporary complementary cash assistance to social benefit recipients who are unable to meet needs. projects.description:
Working at the national and sub-national levels, the output will address the gaps in the access and quality of social services that affect quality of life and exacerbate poverty and vulnerability. In partnership with the national and local authorities, the Programme will focus on improving the delivery of comprehensive programmes and services at central and local levels that respond to humanitarian and long-term recovery needs by strengthening local social protection capacities, mechanisms and structures while delivering essential social assistance. Through the provision of technical assistance and operational support, capacity strengthening, and advocacy support the Programme will ensure the following systemic changes:
•	The Government has increased capacities to operationalize and manage improved social protection programmes that effectively contribute to reduce poverty, integrate and support vulnerable populations (displaced/returnee, Roma) in a gender-responsive and age-appropriate manner, prevent de-institutionalization, and respond to humanitarian crises.
•	Local authorities have improved capacities to plan, finance, implement and monitor child-sensitive, gender-responsive and age-appropriate integrated programmes and have effective and sustainable standards and scalable models for young people’s meaningful participation anchored in the national youth policy and EU youth strategy.
•	The Social Protection System and humanitarian cash actors have enhanced delivery mechanisms at their disposal to provide flexible and shock-effective social assistance during humanitarian emergencies.

projects.description:
The national-level interventions under the Policy output will address systemic inefficiencies causing inadequate quality and access of education for all children, especially the most vulnerable, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. The output will foster resilient, inclusive and gender-transformative educational policies, standards and frameworks, supported by quality disaggregated data and evidence on early childhood, primary and secondary education/vocational education and training, and strengthened digital learning ecosystems anchored in UNICEF’s normative agenda for the protection of children’s rights. 

UNICEF will provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support work to key educational institutions at national and local levels to achieve the following systemic changes: 

Education system has an enabling normative framework for inclusive ECE services (Policy, curriculum framework, minimum quality service standards), which are accountable to the communities they serve. 

The education system is strengthened to provide learning recovery programmes that enable students to catch-up with learning losses and continue formal education.  

Effective system for provision of additional support measures for children with disabilities to facilitate their transition from institutions and inclusion in mainstream schools. 

Knowledge, Attitude, beliefs and behaviour data on student learning and skills development, inclusive education, positive parenting is available and used to inform an equity-driven roll-out of the New Ukrainian School curriculum reform, including the equitable child-focused education recovery plans and budgeting.  

Education system is strengthened to provide for continuity of learning during humanitarian crises. 

General Secondary Schools curricula & assessment frameworks comprehensively address/integrate transferable skills. 

Comprehensive & transparent education data systems are available to inform equity-based decision making at school, hromada, oblast (region) and national levels for implementation of the learning recovery plan and for monitoring and assessment of students learning. 

There is an enabling national-level coordination framework and strategy, aligned with EU systems, to facilitate young people’s transition from school to work.

projects.name: Institutional capacities are strengthened to reform, adopt and implement legislative, regulatory, budgetary and coordination frameworks that enable a quality, risk-informed, age-appropriate, gender-transformative inclusive and shock-responsive child protection system, especially for vulnerable groups.
projects.description:
The national-level interventions under the Policy output will address the systemic gaps and inefficiencies that prevent the child protection system from protecting the Ukrainian children, especially the most vulnerable, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. The outcome will focus on supporting the care reform, fostering mechanisms and policies for child-centered justice and protection and mobilizing partnerships and finance for children to uphold children’s rights in line with UNICEF’s normative agenda. Working with the key state institutions at the national and local levels, UNICEF will spearhead high level policy dialogues and provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support, evidence generation and knowledge sharing, as well as capacity development to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	There is a nationally owned reform strategy and plan for child protection sector reform that is supported by and contributes to humanitarian response, recovery, reconstruction, return and reintegration. 
•	Data and evidence is available to inform child protection and justice sector reforms, policies and programmes and guide Programmes and People agendas.
•	Justice system is equipped with child-centered specialized justice professionals, legislation and referral  and is aligned with the EU standards to protect children in contact with the law.
•	There are frameworks and regulations for effective and shock responsive CPiE and GBViE, including MHPSS and case management, at national and sub-national levels.
•	Monitoring and Reporting Mechanisms are available to inform advocacy/dialogues on grave violations of children’s rights, including the right for family in line with the EU standards.

projects.name: Government has strengthened capacity to reform, adopt and coordinate effective, inclusive, participatory and sustainable shock-responsive social protection policies and budgets for vulnerable children, young people and families.
projects.description:
Through national-level interventions under this Policy output, the programme will focus on systemic inefficiencies that contribute to poverty and vulnerability of Ukrainian children and young people, especially those affected by humanitarian contexts. The programme will focus on strengthening of the Social Protection System of Ukraine, by fostering family-friendly policies, standards and frameworks, supported by quality disaggregated data and evidence on multidimensional and monetary child poverty and sustained by child-centered private and public finance, anchored in UNICEF’s normative agenda for the protection of children’s rights. Working with the key state institutions at the national level, UNICEF will provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support, evidence generation and capacity development to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	There is quality disaggregated data on monetary and multi-dimensional child poverty and deprivations to inform and advocate for child-friendly policies, prioritize children in national budgets and enact and implement inclusive and gender-transformative social protection in Ukraine.
•	The Government is able to draft and enact relevant legislation in line with the EU Chapter on Social Policy, develop flexible and shock-responsive financial mechanisms and operational guidelines for the expansion of SP programmes during the transition phase, design SP programmes that contribute to poverty reduction and an inclusive socio-economic recovery agenda and adopt family friendly policies enabling caregivers to participate in the labour market and contribute to economic recovery while ensuring children’s wellbeing and care.
•	Key financial decision-makers are prepared to prioritize children’s needs, include child-sensitive programmes in national and local budgets and external contributions and make sufficient and sustainable contributions to a child-centred recovery agenda.
•	Interinstitutional coordination is improved for a more effective use of resources within the SPS and with the humanitarian system.
•	Effective and sustainable standards and policies (e.g., youth guarantee, digital MOYS platform, etc.) are available and financed to increase young people’s meaningful participation in line with EU youth strategy.

The output will address the bottlenecks and barriers related to the still prevalent lack of quality data, due to limited capacity to collect and analyze data at all levels and due to the lack of sufficient data interoperability and exchange among data-producing entities. UNICEF also plans to improve availability of recent data on children through support to conduct a MICS, to provide a large household-level dataset which will include internationally comparable estimates of about 130 indicators to assess the situation of children, women and men in the areas of health, education, and child protection. MICS also collects information on about 40 SDG indicators so is a central component to monitoring of SDGs around children. Finally, UNICEF will support a Situation Analysis for Children in preparation for the next country programme cycle, with the aim for joint management and national ownership.

projects.name: Ukrainian authorities have strengthened capacities to develop, coordinate and manage a comprehensive, cross-sectoral monitoring system to uphold children’s rights
projects.description:
Under this Output, UNICEF will work towards the following systemic changes:
•	Nationally owned CRM system to coordinate cross-sectoral monitoring of child rights to ensure children's interests and rights are protected and objectively reflected in decision-making and investments. 
•	Improved skills for evidence-based decision-making investments and independent child rights monitoring.
It will do so through advocacy to establish and strengthen coordination and monitoring mechanisms at national and local levels, and technical assistance to develop frameworks, guidance, standards, tools and standard operating procedures for the cross-sectoral monitoring mechanism. The presence of a fully functional CRM coordinating and monitoring mechanism is key to ensure fulfillment of obligations to implement CRC concluding observations and recommendations. UNICEF will work with government partners to both advocate for establishing and operationalizing the committee and to provide technical assistance to capacitate the committee including standards setting and guidance. The programme will support strengthening of national and local-level capacities and mechanisms for child-rights monitoring and coordination to help the country comply with the CRC recommendations and foster child-centered development.
For both outputs, UNICEF recognizes and supports the need for increased awareness and capacity of rights holders and duty bearers to uphold children’s rights and ensure their realization. This recognizes the role that different segments of society play to ensure the realization of child rights, whether it is the commitment to uphold children’s rights, or the promise to advocate and hold rights holders to account for monitoring and implementing these rights. UNICEF will work across its capacities in child rights monitoring, social and behavior change and communications and advocacy to ensure a coordinated approach to this work.
The outcome operates under the assumption that the achievement of the results will be conditional on the regular production of child-related data by the State Statistics Service, including production of SDG data and updating of the TransMonEE database. It’s also contingent on the commitment of the government to maintain the harmonized/cross-sectoral child-related data management system and to establish and maintain a national CRM system at all levels. Risks specific to this outcome include de-prioritization of evidence and statistics functions within the limited fiscal space and resulting lack of adequate buy-in and resourcing in data and evidence systems. Other risks are that the constraints on statistical functions related to martial law impact the conduct of household surveys such as MICS.

projects.name: Rapidly restore local cereal, vegetable and livestock production as immediate source of food and income, with a focus on women
projects.description:
Improved access to agricultural inputs through voucher-based assistance, enabling farming households and small farmers to procure certified seeds, fertilizers, tools, and small-scale machinery. 

To support the restoration and sustainability of crop production, FAO will provide small-scale farmers with access to essential agricultural inputs such as certified seeds, fertilizers, hand tools, and small-scale machinery. This assistance will be delivered through a voucher-based modality, which enhances beneficiary choice, promotes efficiency, and strengthens local input markets. The voucher approach enables farmers to procure inputs tailored to their specific agro-ecological conditions and farming practices, while also ensuring access to quality-assured products from vetted local suppliers. This modality has proven effective in Mykolaivska and Khersonska oblasts, where FAO has established a reliable supplier network. Post-distribution monitoring (PDM) indicates strong preference for vouchers due to their relevance, quality, and convenience. This intervention contributes to improved agricultural productivity, supports rural market systems, and reinforces the resilience of conflict-affected farming communities. A value-for-money (VfM) analysis of FAO’s potato and vegetables seeds package as well as vouchers for agriculture input found that an investment in seeds and agricultural inputs yielded 755 kg of potato and vegetable products worth US$ 404. The intervention triples returns, boosts self-sufficiency, reduces aid dependence and improves mental health in crisis-affected households.

projects.name: Safeguarding Independent Media and Information Integrity in Ukraine: Emergency Response and Sustainable Recovery
projects.description:
The main goal of this project is to support new critical and emerging needs in the fields of safety of journalists, media viability, and access to trustworthy information in Ukraine – including on recovery efforts. Beyond the tragic loss of life, the war continues to destroy media infrastructure, disrupt income sources, affect journalists’ livelihoods and equipment, and cause staffing shortages. Many journalists have been displaced, and media professionals, especially women, are dealing with gender-based threats, both online and offline. To address the urgent needs identified, work will be conducted under the following three outcomes: 
Outcome 1: The safety and resilience of journalists, media workers, and freedom-of-expression defenders are strengthened through emergency assistance, psychological support, with a strong gender-sensitive approach.
Outcome 2: The viability of Ukrainian media outlets is advanced through support for sustainable business models development and tailored audience outreach.
Outcome 3: Access to reliable information is reinforced through the promotion of international standards on freedom of expression, information integrity, and enhanced media and information literacy, with a particular emphasis on civil servants and judicial actors.

By continuing supporting the safety of journalists and the recovery of the media sector, the project will help ensure that the Ukrainian people receive reliable information in the times of war.

Additionally, it will facilitate knowledge-sharing between Ukrainian and international media experts to strengthen the sector’s role in promoting transparency in the recovery process. projects.description:
FAO aims to strengthen gender equality in Ukraine’s agricultural sector through a multi-pronged approach. This includes:

National Advocacy and Community Engagement: FAO will launch a nationwide campaign to improve women’s access to agricultural support, especially in frontline oblasts.

Gender Mainstreaming Trainings: At the request of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine (MAPF), FAO is conducting strategic sessions and workshops to build capacity among policymakers and practitioners. These sessions explore practical tools, challenges, and best practices for integrating gender into agricultural policy.

Country Gender Assessment (CGA): FAO is updating its CGA to reflect the evolving roles of women in agriculture since the full-scale war and displacement began in 2022. The assessment applies an intersectional lens and will offer gender-transformative recommendations to guide future programming and investments. It is scheduled for completion by September 2025.

Gender-Responsive Policy Development: FAO is training at least 40 MAPF staff (with 50% female participation) to enhance gender-sensitive policy formulation and implementation .

Inclusive SAR Registration: FAO is working to identify and address barriers that prevent women—who currently represent less than 5% of registered users—from accessing the State Agrarian Register (SAR). This includes targeted outreach and platform accessibility studies .

Operational Gender Sensitivity: All implementing partners are trained on SEA prevention, GBV principles, and gender-sensitive communication. Project data is disaggregated by sex, and monitoring tools ensure equitable treatment throughout the project cycle .

Field-Level Inclusion: In grain storage operations, FAO prioritized women-led applications and engaged female laborers in post-harvest activities. For example, 65% of laborers hired during the Canadian fiscal year were women

projects.description:
Diesel generators distributed to agro producers and processors in war-affected oblasts to ensure continuity of agricultural operations and food system resilience.

In response to Ukraine’s escalating energy crisis and its impact on agri-food systems, FAO launched a targeted intervention to provide diesel generators to vulnerable agro producers and processors. The strategy prioritized regions facing frequent power outages and businesses receiving humanitarian aid for the first time. Through close collaboration with MAPF, FAO ensured transparent selection criteria and equitable distribution across oblasts such as Khersonska, Donetska, Mykolaivska, and Sumska. The generators—ranging from 75 to 110 kW—are deploying to support critical operations including dairy and meat processing, grain cultivation, fisheries, and organic farming. This intervention not only enable uninterrupted production and service delivery but also laid the foundation for long-term resilience and recovery in Ukraine’s rural economy.

projects.name: Culture as a tool of resilience: Using the power of culture to heal emotional and psychological trauma
projects.description: Due to the impact of the war on livelihoods and the disruption of the transmission of living heritage across Ukraine, widespread physical, emotional and psychological trauma amongst local communities. Recognizing that the arts and humanities can act as tools for social healing and inclusion, the HEF enabled the delivery of support for art therapy activities by facilitating the development of a methodological framework and multimodal curriculum which integrates local cultural practices and the best international mental health approaches to promote the healing and resilience of targeted groups encompassing children aged 6-14, youth aged 15-21, family members of the participating children and youth, veterans, IDPs, volunteers, and educators. The resulting rehabilitation programme was called “Art for Life”. On 29-31 July 2024, a 3-day training for 16 psychologists and psychotherapists (all women) was held in Bryukhovychi, Lviv region, to update their knowledge in the field of art therapy, familiarize them with the features of the “Art for Life” programme and certify them to participate in its deployment. Additional online seminars were developed in August and September 2024 for all participants.
